subject: Finly discovery recap — p95 latency & concurrency (streaming)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@finly.com>, Asha Singh <asha.singh@finly.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Ethan Park <ethan@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, Apr 1, 2027 at 4:05 PM PDT
Subject: Finly discovery recap — p95 latency & concurrency (streaming)

Thanks for taking the time earlier today — great to meet the Finly team. Quick recap from our call so we have alignment on pain, goals, and immediate next steps. Please reply with any corrections.

High-level pain & context:
- Production UX degradation during peak trading hours: user-facing chat and search features see p95 generation latency spikes that cause the streaming UI to stall and users to refresh.
- Current stack: model hosting on AWS SageMaker endpoints running a mix of 13B/70B variants (mixed precision), in-region across us-west-2. No prefix KV cache in front of the endpoints; per-request cold-starts and micro-batching are hand-tuned.
- Observed behavior: p95 for short responses (~<64 tokens) is ~850ms-.2s during peaks; average token emit gap during streaming is 120-250ms which creates a choppy UX.

Success criteria (what Finly needs from a pilot):
1) P95 latency for short completions (<64 tokens) consistently <250ms under steady-state load (baseline target).
2) Streaming partials emitted with <100ms token gaps for low-latency conversational UX.
3) Sustained concurrency: handle 300 concurrent streaming sessions with graceful degradation and fallbacks (no hard errors).
4) Clear cost / throughput tradeoffs and recommended quantization or batching profile to hit (1)-(3).

Other constraints:
- Security: SOC2 evidence will be required for production pilot (Asha is owner).
- Procurement timeline: Finly is targeting procurement sign-off by end of Q2.

Technical notes / observations from the call:
- Aditya: Finly uses a hybrid routing layer that pins some traffic to bigger models for complex queries; we discussed model variants and transparent fallback to smaller quantized variants.
- Ethan: asked about streaming SDK and early-token flush behavior; Finly wants partials visible as soon as possible (server push + chunked encoding acceptable).

Next steps (agreed):
- Redwood to run a scoped benchmark: we will mirror a 15-minute peak traffic window from Finly (you’ll share a representative traffic trace + sample prompts). Deliverable: p95/avg latency, partial emission timing, and throughput/cost estimates. (Owner: Aditya; ETA: 7 business days)
- Finly to share anonymized traffic trace and a small prompt set (~200 prompts) plus a target workload profile (concurrency curve). (Owner: Samir/Asha; ETA: 3 business days)
- Schedule follow-up tech deep dive to review benchmark results and pilot contract terms. Proposed time: week of Apr 12. (Owner: Marissa)

Attachments: redwood-discovery-deck.pdf (pilot proposal + architecture), p95-benchmarking.csv (example output format).

Thanks — looking forward to the trace.


Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | (650) 555-0193
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Finly discovery recap — p95 latency & concurrency (streaming)

Thanks Marissa — this is an accurate capture. A few clarifications and asks from our side: 

1) Prompts & trace: we'll export a 20-minute window that includes the 7-9am spike and sanitize personal data. Expect the link by Monday.
2) Baseline hardware: the current SageMaker hosts are g5.12xlarge and a small pool of p4dn for heavy workloads; we'll include instance types in the trace metadata.
3) Procurement/cost question: can Redwood provide a ballpark monthly run-rate for the pilot (staging + 2-week ramp + production sim) so we can model quickly? Even a range is helpful.
4) Security: Asha will send the SOC2 checklist and questions today — can you confirm who on Redwood's side is primary for security evidence?

We'll prioritize the trace export this week. Procurement is optimistic for end-of-June sign-off but we may need a short POC to unblock legal.


Samir Gupta
Head of Infrastructure, Finly
samir.gupta@finly.com
